messages.subject: R crashing with new installation of R-2.14.1 and latest aroma.affymetrix
parts:
Hi all,

I installed R-2.14.1 yesterday on my Mac Pro running OS X 10.6.8
using the Mac R-2.14.1.pkg installer downloaded from CRAN.

I then installed the latest aroma.affymetrix using
source("http://aroma-project.org/hbLite.R");
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix");

and affymetrix packages from Bioconductor.

I've hit a reproducible problem running code that was working
before I updated.

The commands that crash R are

> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6", tags = "Full")
> print(cdf)

Process R abort trap at Fri Jan 13 12:02:33 2012

Full session information below.

The R session crashes completely without any R abort choices.

This happens running the above commands either in an Emacs R session
or if I run the same commands in the R GUI.

Any recommendations as to how to proceed or to further
report this problem would be appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] R crashing with new installation of R-2.14.1 and latest aroma.affymetrix
parts:
Hi,

I'm pretty sure this is due to the OSX specific problem where the
Bioconductor build of the affxparser package causes R to crash, cf.
Bioc-devel thread 'affxparser: Core dump with R 2.14.0 on OSX' on Nov
7, 2011:

https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/bioc-devel/2011-November/002969.html

I know that Kasper Hansen tried to help BioC to track this down. From
what he told me and from the above thread, the Bioconductor builds for
affxparser v1.26.2 are faulty for OSX 10.6 ("Snow Leopard"), and OSX
10.7 ("Lion"), but not for OSX 10.5 ("Leopard"). Since it is likely
that it has to do with the BioC build system that runs R v2.14.x, it
may work with previous affxparser builds. See if installing the
affxparser v1.24.0 from BioC v2.8 (previous release) works:

library("R.utils");
installPackages("http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.8/bioc/bin/macosx/leopard/contrib/2.13/affxparser_1.24.0.tgz");

You can try the example I posted in the above thread (you can download
and unzip the CDF from
http://www.aroma-project.org/data/annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Nsp/):

> library("affxparser");
> library("digest");
> pathname <- "annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Nsp/Mapping250K_Nsp.cdf";
> fi <- file.info(pathname);
> rownames(fi) <- NULL;
> print(fi);
> print(digest(file=pathname));
> print(sessionInfo());
> hdr <- readCdfHeader(pathname);
> str(hdr);

Let us if workaround helps, because your not the only one having this problem.

/Henrik

Hi,

I'm pretty sure this is due to the OSX specific problem where the
Bioconductor build of the affxparser package causes R to crash, cf.
Bioc-devel thread 'affxparser: Core dump with R 2.14.0 on OSX' on Nov
7, 2011:

https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/bioc-devel/2011-November/002969.html

I know that Kasper Hansen tried to help BioC to track this down. From
what he told me and from the above thread, the Bioconductor builds for
affxparser v1.26.2 are faulty for OSX 10.6 ("Snow Leopard"), and OSX
10.7 ("Lion"), but not for OSX 10.5 ("Leopard"). Since it is likely
that it has to do with the BioC build system that runs R v2.14.x, it
may work with previous affxparser builds. See if installing the
affxparser v1.24.0 from BioC v2.8 (previous release) works:

library("R.utils");
installPackages("http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.8/bioc/bin/macosx/leopard/contrib/2.13/affxparser_1.24.0.tgz");

You can try the example I posted in the above thread (you can download
and unzip the CDF from
http://www.aroma-project.org/data/annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Nsp/):

> library("affxparser");
> library("digest");
> pathname <- "annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Nsp/Mapping250K_Nsp.cdf";
> fi <- file.info(pathname);
> rownames(fi) <- NULL;
> print(fi);
> print(digest(file=pathname));
> print(sessionInfo());
> hdr <- readCdfHeader(pathname);
> str(hdr);

Let us if workaround helps, because your not the only one having this problem.

/Henrik
